summary:
I've been building Keikochō, a Japanese-learning app I use myself, and lately the interesting work has been noticing when the app is lying to me about what it's teaching. The dojo (its grammar practice mode) presented multiple-choice comprehension questions that looked like they tested grammar, but I found 88% of them were solvable just from the English answer choices — pick the one with a question mark and you're done, no Japanese required. I rebuilt the item so the prompt is in English and the tiles you pick from are Japanese; that dropped the solve-without-reading rate to zero, verified against a sweep I run automatically now so it can't quietly creep back up.

A second one: I asked the app for time-telling practice and it quizzed me on "seven o'clock" before ever teaching me what "seven" meant. The bug was that the app only checked whether I could read the kana, never whether I'd actually been introduced to the word — two different questions that happened to line up until I added new content that outran the teaching order. Fixed by adding an explicit step that meets a word before the pool ever quizzes on it.

On the image side, I've been generating art for word cards with a couple of different models and learned some very specific things the hard way: Stable-Diffusion-style models can't count past about six before rounding to whatever grid looks symmetric, so "seven balls" comes back as six or nine depending on the seed. Flux (a different model, via Replicate) counts correctly if you describe a shape instead of a number — "one straight row of seven" works, "seven balls" doesn't.

Separately, I set up SwarmUI as a real front end for image generation — seed locking, negative prompts, sampler control — sitting in front of an existing ComfyUI backend rather than running its own. Getting there took chasing down a few landmines: pinning it to an older release because the current one imports a node the backend doesn't have, and working around it trying to write metadata into model files that live on a read-only mount.

highlights.oneLiner: Generating word-card art via SD and Flux; building SwarmUI as a front end with seed lock and negative prompts
